subject: Data Processing
examFormat: Two papers taken as a composite paper at one sitting. Paper 1: forty multiple-choice objective questions, all to be answered in 1 hour for 40 marks. Paper 2 has Sections A and B and candidates answer five questions in all. Section A: four essay questions, any three to be answered in 1 hour for 30 marks. Section B: a test of practical work with two compulsory essay questions, to be answered in 1 hour for 40 marks.

topics.name: History of Computers
objectives: Identify computing devices since the beginning of counting/computing
Explain the importance of number systems to computing
Describe the first to fifth generations of computers (year of development, basic component/type of technology, speed of operation, storage capacity/component)
topics.content: Concept of number system in computing; generations of computer: first, second, third, fourth and fifth. Each generation is related to its characteristic features.

topics.name: Data and Information
topics.content: Differences between data and information should be emphasized.

topics.name: Classification of Computers
objectives: Classify computers by type, size and usage

topics.name: Application of ICT in Everyday Life
objectives: Describe the uses of ICT in everyday activities
Explain the impact of ICT on society
topics.content: The use and areas of ICT application should be linked to societal development.

topics.name: Components of Computers
topics.content: Examples of each component should be treated, and how they are used in data processing.

topics.name: The Art of Information Processing
objectives: Describe the steps involved in information processing
topics.content: Description of each step involved in information processing is required.

topics.name: Process of Information Transmission
topics.content: Modes of information transmission such as visual (newspaper), audio (radio, telephone) and audio-visual (GSM, television) are required.

topics.name: Medium of Information Transmission
objectives: Identify the types of information transmission
topics.content: Media of information transmission such as radio, television, newspaper, etc.

topics.name: Networking
objectives: Explain the meaning of networking, Internet and Intranet
topics.content: The significance of networking should be mentioned. Types such as MAN, LAN and WAN should be treated.

topics.name: Internet
objectives: State the benefits of the Internet
Develop skills in the use of various services available on the Internet

topics.name: Operating System
objectives: Identify the types of operating system
State the functions of an operating system
topics.content: Differences between text (character) based interface and Graphical User Interface should be treated.

topics.name: Word Processing
objectives: State the uses of word processing
Give examples of word processing software
Start, load and exit word processing
Use a word processor to create and manipulate documents

topics.name: Spreadsheet
objectives: Create, save and retrieve spreadsheet files
Use a spreadsheet to create and manipulate worksheets

topics.name: Database Management System
objectives: Create, save and retrieve database files
Use a DBMS to create and manipulate database files
topics.content: Include examples of packages for database management such as Microsoft Access.

topics.name: Presentation Package
objectives: Define presentation packages, their uses and examples
Create, save and retrieve presentation files
Use presentation programs to create and manipulate slides

topics.name: Web Design Packages
objectives: Give examples of web design packages
topics.content: Designing of web pages is not required.

topics.name: Graphic Packages
objectives: State the uses of graphic software packages
topics.content: Focus should be placed on Corel Draw.

topics.name: Maintenance of Computer
objectives: Describe battery charging and replacement for portable systems and UPS
Explain computer crash and data recovery
topics.content: Candidates should take note of basic maintenance procedures and should be able to ensure data integrity and recover data after a crash.

topics.name: Computer Ethics
topics.content: Responsible ways of using and securing computers.

topics.name: Safety Measures
objectives: Describe the positioning of the monitor, keyboard, CPU, mouse and other peripheral devices
Explain the illumination of the computer room
Explain how to maintain a dust-free environment
Explain why liquids should be kept away from the computer room
topics.content: The importance of safety measures should be emphasized.

topics.name: Career Opportunities in Data Processing
objectives: State the qualities of a good data processing professional
topics.content: The duties of each professional and professional body should be treated.

topics.name: Computer Virus
objectives: Describe virus prevention, detection and deletion
topics.content: Destructive effects of virus infection on computers.

topics.name: Relational Model
objectives: Create databases and tables using application packages
topics.content: Arranging data in tables and forms should be emphasized. The concepts of primary and foreign keys, entities, attributes and relationships should be emphasized. Query language should be limited to those available to the database application package (e.g. query by example, SQL).

topics.name: File Organization
objectives: Identify the types of file organization
Compare the various types of file organization

topics.name: Database Security
objectives: Explain the concept of data security, access control and data encryption
Describe the role of a database administrator
topics.content: The importance of securing data is required.

topics.name: Parallel and Distributed Databases
objectives: Explain the basic concept of parallel and distributed databases
Describe storing data in a distributed database (DBM)
topics.content: Definitions of concepts are required. The significance of storing data in a distributed database management system is also required.
